class.name: GameModeBase
class.brief_description: The rules of a level, and the scenes everything else is built from.
class.description: It exists on the server only: it decides who may join, where they spawn and when the match is over. The list of players everyone is allowed to see lives on the [GameStateBase] instead. A game mode is a scene whose root is a [GameModeBase], pointed at by [member Level.game_mode_override] or by the [code]application/game_framework/default_game_mode[/code] project setting. Its default scenes - [member game_state_scene], [member player_state_scene], [member player_controller_scene], [member default_pawn_scene] - are read on a client too, without the game mode ever being part of that client's world: both sides have to build the same things for a player. Override [code]_init_game[/code] to set the level up (return [code]true[/code] to take spawning over completely), [code]_pre_login[/code] to refuse a connecting peer, [code]_on_post_login[/code] and [code]_on_logout[/code] to follow players in and out, and [code]_get_pawn_scene_for[/code] to choose a pawn per player.

method.name: _can_join
method.description: Override to refuse a press-to-join from [param device_slot]. This is where [i]two pads only, ignore the keyboard[/i] belongs: compare against [constant PlayerInput.DEVICE_SLOT_KEYBOARD_MOUSE].

method.name: _choose_player_start
method.description: Override to pick where a player appears. Return a start node, or null to fall back to the default search.

method.name: _get_pawn_scene_for
method.description: Override to choose a pawn per controller - a class selection, a vehicle. [b]Return a scene, not a spawned node[/b]: naming a scene is what lets every peer build the same pawn.

method.name: _init_game
method.description: Override to prepare the level before anyone is spawned. [b]Return [code]true[/code] to suppress the player spawn entirely[/b] - that is how a menu level runs with no player at all rather than with an empty one. Return [code]false[/code] and the framework logs the local players in and possesses their pawns on its own. Prepare here, play in [code]_ready[/code].

method.name: _init_game_state
method.description: Override for setup that runs after the game state exists and before any player is logged in.

method.name: _on_logout
method.description: Override to react to a player leaving, before their nodes are freed.

method.name: _on_post_login
method.description: Override to react to a player arriving, with their controller, player state and pawn already built.

method.name: _pre_login
method.description: Override to vet a connecting peer. Return an error message to refuse it - the reason reaches the client through [signal login_refused] - or an empty string to let it in.

method.name: choose_player_start
method.description: Picks an unclaimed start for [param controller], asking [method _choose_player_start] first. [b]Starts are claimed once each per level[/b]: with more players than starts the framework warns and reuses them, and it cannot test whether a start is physically occupied.

method.name: find_player_start
method.description: The first start whose [member PlayerStart2D.player_start_tag] matches, or null.

method.name: get_num_players
method.description: How many players are in the match.

method.name: get_pawn_scene_for
method.description: The pawn scene for [param controller], asking [method _get_pawn_scene_for] first and falling back to [method get_pawn_scene_for_player].

method.name: get_pawn_scene_for_player
method.description: The pawn scene for local player [param player_index]: its [member pawn_scene_overrides] entry, or [member default_pawn_scene].

method.name: get_player_controller_at
method.description: The controller at [param index], or null.

method.name: get_player_controllers
method.description: Every player controller the server holds.

method.name: get_world
method.description: The world this game mode belongs to.

method.name: login_local_player
method.description: Creates the controller, the player state and a pawn for one human at this machine, and returns the controller.

method.name: login_peer
method.description: The same as [method login_local_player], for a player at another machine - called once that machine has reported the level up, never before.

method.name: logout
method.description: Removes a player: their pawn, their controller and their player state.

method.name: logout_peer
method.description: Logs out every player on connection [param peer_id].

method.name: restart_all_players
method.description: Logs in every local player that has no controller yet, up to [member max_local_players].

method.name: restart_player
method.description: Spawns a fresh pawn at a chosen start and possesses it - a respawn.

method.name: restart_player_at
method.description: As [method restart_player], but at [param start_spot] rather than a chosen one.

method.name: spawn_default_player
method.description: Ensures local player 0 exists, logs it in and returns its controller. This is what runs by default when [method _init_game] returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: start_play
method.description: Marks the match as begun and lets every peer know, through [signal GameStateBase.begun_play].

method.name: try_join
method.description: Offers [param device_slot] to press-to-join. The [InputRouter] calls this when a device nobody owns is pressed; a player already in the game but holding no device claims it first, which is what makes the same path double as picking a pad back up after a disconnect. Returns whether anyone took it.

members.member: When true, a button on a device no player owns logs a new local player in, up to [member max_local_players]. Gate it further with [method _can_join].

The pawn every player gets, unless [member pawn_scene_overrides] or [method _get_pawn_scene_for] says otherwise. It has to be its own file: [b]a scene built inline cannot be named to another machine[/b], so a client would have nothing to build.
The scene built as this level's [GameStateBase]. Its root must be one. Read on clients too, so both sides build the same thing.

How many humans may share this machine. Leaving it at 1 keeps player 0 accepting every device, exactly as the global input singleton always did. [b]Raising it without narrowing player 0 off [constant PlayerInput.DEVICE_SLOT_ALL] leaves nothing for anyone else[/b] - the framework warns about that combination.
How many players the session accepts, counting everyone on every machine.
Per-local-player pawn scenes, indexed by local player index. Falls back to [member default_pawn_scene] when the array is short or the entry is null.
The scene built for each player's [PlayerController]. Its root must be one.
The scene built for each player's [PlayerState]. Its root must be one.

signal.name: login_refused
signal.description: A connecting peer was turned away, with the reason [method _pre_login] gave.

signal.name: player_logged_in
signal.description: A player joined and their controller exists.

signal.name: player_restarted
signal.description: A player got a fresh pawn.
